tests.overview: IELTS (International English Language Testing System) is the world's most popular English language proficiency test for higher education and migration. It is jointly managed by the British Council, IDP: IELTS Australia, and Cambridge Assessment English. Available in Academic and General Training modules, it uses a 9-band scoring system.
tests.format: Four sections: Listening (30 min + 10 min transfer), Reading (60 min), Writing (60 min, 2 tasks), Speaking (11-14 min, face-to-face interview). Available in Computer-delivered (results in 3-5 days) and Paper-based (results in 13 days) formats.
tests.scoring: 9-band scale (0-9). Each section gets a band score; overall is average of all four, rounded to nearest 0.5. Band 9 = Expert User, Band 6 = Competent User.
registrationSteps: Create account on British Council (britishcouncil.pk) or IDP (ielts.idp.com) or AEO
Choose test type: Academic or General Training
Pay test fee (PKR 75,600-76,240 for computer; varies by city)
Receive confirmation email 5-7 days before test
testDay: Bring valid passport or CNIC used during registration
Arrive at least 30 minutes before scheduled time
Listening, Reading, Writing completed same day (no break)
Speaking may be on same day or within 7 days (for paper-based)
Computer-delivered Speaking is usually same day at different time
tests.resultsTimeline: Computer-delivered: 3-5 business days. Paper-based: 13 calendar days.
tests.scoreSending: One TRF (Test Report Form) included. Additional TRFs cost extra. Electronic delivery available to 5 institutions.
tests.accommodations: Special arrangements available for candidates with disabilities (visual, hearing, or physical). Must request during registration with supporting medical documentation.
tests.retakePolicy: Can retake as many times as needed. No waiting period between attempts.
tests.preparationTimeline: Recommended 4-8 weeks of focused preparation. Daily practice of all four skills recommended.
commonMistakes: Booking Academic when you need UKVI (for UK visa applicants)
Not matching registration document to what you bring on test day
Booking paper-based when deadline is close (results take 13 days)
Ignoring the Speaking test date (may be separate for paper-based)

tests.overview: TOEFL iBT (Test of English as a Foreign Language, internet-Based Testing) is developed by ETS and measures academic English skills across reading, listening, speaking, and writing. As of January 2026, TOEFL uses a new adaptive format with a 1-6 scoring scale aligned to CEFR.
tests.format: Adaptive test with four sections: Reading, Listening, Speaking, Writing. Total test time approximately 2 hours. Reading and Listening are two-stage adaptive. Speaking and Writing use AI scoring with human verification.
tests.scoring: New 1-6 scale (half-point increments) aligned to CEFR, effective January 2026. For a 2-year transition period, also reports 0-120 comparable score. Section scores: Reading, Listening, Speaking, Writing each on 1-6 scale.
registrationSteps: Select test type: TOEFL iBT at test center or Home Edition
Pay registration fee (USD 200-250, varies by country)
testDay: Bring valid passport with matching name
Arrive 30 minutes early at test center
Unofficial scores for Reading and Listening available immediately
Official scores available in 8-10 business days
tests.resultsTimeline: 8-10 business days for official scores. Unofficial Reading/Listening scores available immediately after test.
tests.scoreSending: 4 free score reports included. Additional reports: USD 29 each. Can select recipients before or after test.
tests.accommodations: Extensive disability accommodations available. Must submit request with documentation before registration deadline.
tests.retakePolicy: Can retake with no waiting period between attempts. Maximum 1 attempt per 3-day period.
tests.preparationTimeline: Recommended 2-3 months of preparation. Official ETS prep materials highly recommended.
commonMistakes: Confusing old 0-120 scale with new 1-6 scale (both appear on score report)
Not practicing with official TOEFL prep materials
Underestimating the adaptive nature of Reading and Listening
Forgetting to select score recipients during registration

Accepted by most universities

tests.scoring: Score range 400-1600. Each section scored 200-800. Total is sum of both section scores.

tests.accommodations: College Board provides accommodations for students with documented disabilities. Must apply in advance.
tests.retakePolicy: Can retake as many times as desired. Superscoring policy: highest section scores across attempts are combined.
tests.preparationTimeline: Recommended 2-3 months. Free official practice tests available through Khan Academy.
commonMistakes: Not downloading and testing Bluebook app before test day

tests.overview: The ACT is a standardized test for college admissions in the United States, covering English, Math, Reading, and Science. It is an alternative to the SAT.
tests.format: Four required sections: English (45 min, 75 questions), Math (60 min, 60 questions), Reading (35 min, 40 questions), Science (35 min, 40 questions). Optional Writing test (40 min, 1 essay). Total: 2 hours 55 min (without Writing) or 3 hours 35 min (with Writing).
tests.scoring: Score range 1-36 for each section. Composite score is average of four section scores, rounded to nearest whole number.
registrationSteps: Pay fee (approximately USD 68 without Writing, USD 93 with Writing)
International students pay additional USD 68 surcharge
testDay: Bring admission ticket and valid photo ID
Calculator permitted on Math section (check approved list)
tests.scoreSending: Up to 4 free score reports. Additional reports: USD 18 each.
tests.accommodations: Available for students with documented disabilities. Must apply in advance.
tests.retakePolicy: Can retake multiple times. ACT superscores across attempts.
